interactions.label: Which layer of the glomerular filtration barrier is primarily responsible for pr

params.question: Which layer of the glomerular filtration barrier is primarily responsible for preventing albumin from crossing into the filtrate through charge repulsion?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The fenestrated endothelium has pores of 70–100 nm that restrict blood cells and large proteins mainly by size. It does not provide a significant charge barrier.
Correct. The GBM carries a strong negative charge. Since albumin is also negatively charged, the two repel each other — this is the primary charge-selective barrier of the glomerulus.
The slit diaphragm, bridged by nephrin protein, acts as the final size-selective barrier. Its role is structural rather than charge-based.
The parietal epithelium lines the outer wall of Bowman's capsule. It is not part of the three-layer filtration barrier between capillary blood and the capsular space.

overallFeedback.feedback: The glomerular basement membrane is the charge-selective layer. Its negative charge repels albumin, which is also negatively charged. When diabetes damages the GBM, albumin leaks through and proteinuria results.
Well done! The GBM's negative charge repels negatively charged albumin — explaining why glycation damage in diabetic nephropathy leads to proteinuria.

interactions.label: In tubuloglomerular feedback, when GFR rises and sodium chloride delivery to the

params.question: In tubuloglomerular feedback, when GFR rises and sodium chloride delivery to the macula densa increases, which substance is released to constrict the afferent arteriole?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Renin is released when GFR falls and NaCl delivery to the macula densa decreases. It activates the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system to restore filtration — the opposite scenario.
Nitric oxide is a vasodilator that would increase, not decrease, blood flow to the glomerulus. It does not mediate the constrictive response of tubuloglomerular feedback.
Correct. When NaCl rises at the macula densa, adenosine is released. In the kidney (unlike most tissues), adenosine constricts the afferent arteriole, reducing GFR back towards normal.
Angiotensin II is generated downstream of renin release and primarily constricts the efferent arteriole. It is not directly released by the macula densa in response to high NaCl.

overallFeedback.feedback: When GFR is too high, elevated NaCl at the macula densa triggers adenosine release. Adenosine constricts the afferent arteriole, reducing glomerular blood flow and bringing GFR back to normal — a classic negative-feedback loop.
Excellent! Adenosine uniquely constricts the afferent arteriole in the kidney, forming a negative-feedback loop that stabilises GFR despite blood pressure changes.

interactions.label: In a patient with uncontrolled diabetes and plasma glucose of 300 mg/dL, what is

params.question: In a patient with uncontrolled diabetes and plasma glucose of 300 mg/dL, what is the primary mechanism by which glucosuria leads to increased urine output?

answers.text: Unabsorbed glucose in the tubular lumen acts as an osmotic solute, retaining water and preventing its reabsorption

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Once SGLT2 transporters are saturated (above the Tm of 375 mg/min), glucose remaining in the lumen holds water by osmosis, causing the osmotic diuresis and polyuria characteristic of uncontrolled diabetes.

answers.text: Glucose directly stimulates the NKCC2 co-transporter in the thick ascending limb, increasing solute excretion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: NKCC2 handles sodium, potassium, and chloride reabsorption in the loop of Henle. Glucose does not interact with this transporter. The diuresis is osmotic, not transporter-mediated at this site.

answers.text: High plasma glucose inhibits ADH release from the posterior pituitary, reducing water reabsorption

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ADH deficiency causes diabetes insipidus, a separate condition. In diabetes mellitus, osmotic diuresis occurs because glucose itself draws water into the tubular lumen, not because ADH secretion is impaired.

answers.text: Excess glucose damages aquaporin-2 channels in the collecting duct wall

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Aquaporin-2 channels are regulated by ADH, not directly damaged by glucose. The polyuria in diabetes mellitus results from the osmotic effect of unabsorbed glucose in the proximal tubule and loop.

overallFeedback.feedback: When plasma glucose exceeds the renal threshold (180 mg/dL), SGLT2 transporters saturate. The unabsorbed glucose holds water in the tubule by osmosis, producing the polyuria, dehydration, and thirst of uncontrolled diabetes.
Well done! Osmotic diuresis is the hallmark of hyperglycaemia — once the Tm is exceeded, glucose acts as an osmotic particle that retains water in the tubular lumen.

interactions.label: Bicarbonate reabsorption in the proximal convoluted tubule directly excretes aci

params.question: Bicarbonate reabsorption in the proximal convoluted tubule directly excretes acid from the body.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Bicarbonate reabsorption recovers filtered bicarbonate from the tubular lumen — it prevents bicarbonate loss but does not remove acid from the body. The actual acid excretion mechanisms are titratable acidity (via phosphate) and ammonium excretion (from glutamine), the latter of which can increase tenfold in chronic acidosis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Well recognised. Proximal tubule bicarbonate reabsorption recovers filtered bicarbonate and returns it to the blood, but it does not generate new bicarbonate or excrete hydrogen ions from the body. True acid excretion occurs through titratable acidity (phosphate buffering) and ammonium excretion (glutamine pathway), which can scale up tenfold in chronic acidosis.

interactions.label: Why does creatinine clearance slightly overestimate the true glomerular filtrati

params.question: Why does creatinine clearance slightly overestimate the true glomerular filtration rate?

answers.text: Creatinine is partially reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Creatinine is not significantly reabsorbed. If it were, less creatinine would appear in the urine and clearance would underestimate GFR, not overestimate it.

answers.text: Creatinine is not freely filtered at the glomerulus due to its molecular size

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Creatinine (molecular weight ~113 Da) is freely filtered at the glomerulus. If filtration were restricted, clearance would be lower than GFR, not higher.

answers.text: Plasma creatinine levels fluctuate too rapidly for accurate measurement

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Serum creatinine is relatively stable in steady state. The overestimation is a physiological phenomenon related to tubular handling, not a measurement artefact.

answers.text: Creatinine is secreted by the tubules in addition to being filtered

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The proximal tubule actively secretes creatinine into the lumen. Since total urinary creatinine equals filtered plus secreted, the calculated clearance exceeds the true GFR by about 10–15%.

overallFeedback.feedback: Creatinine is both freely filtered and actively secreted by the proximal tubule. Because secretion adds extra creatinine to the urine, the clearance formula yields a value slightly higher than the true GFR measured by inulin.

Excellent! Tubular secretion adds extra creatinine to the urine beyond what filtration alone would produce. That is why inulin clearance (no secretion, no reabsorption) remains the gold standard for measuring GFR.

interactions.label: A patient with syndrome of inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) presents with sev

params.question: A patient with syndrome of inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) presents with severe hyponatraemia. Which class of diuretic specifically addresses this condition by blocking the vasopressin receptor?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Loop diuretics block NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb and increase water excretion indirectly. They do not target the ADH pathway specifically and are not the first-line treatment for SIADH.
Thiazides block the NaCl co-transporter in the distal convoluted tubule. They can actually worsen hyponatraemia by impairing the kidney's diluting ability — the opposite of what this patient needs.

Correct. Tolvaptan blocks the V2 vasopressin receptor in the collecting duct, preventing aquaporin-2 insertion. This promotes free water excretion, directly counteracting the excess ADH activity in SIADH.
Spironolactone blocks the aldosterone receptor in the collecting duct, affecting sodium and potassium handling. It does not target ADH-mediated water reabsorption.

overallFeedback.feedback: Vaptans (e.g., tolvaptan) block the V2 vasopressin receptor in the collecting duct, preventing aquaporin-2 channel insertion. By promoting free water excretion without sodium loss, they directly treat the water retention and hyponatraemia of SIADH.

Well done! Vaptans directly antagonise ADH at the V2 receptor, preventing aquaporin-2 insertion and promoting selective free water excretion — the targeted treatment for dilutional hyponatraemia in SIADH.
